messages:
Alice Nguyen: Quick thread — microbatch scaling for the new azure-embed-lite-v2 bring-up. I flipped on microbatching + dynamic padding on the GPU cluster and saw a small but consistent recall@10 drop.
Mateo Garcia: Can you share numbers? rough delta and config?
Alice Nguyen: Baseline (no microbatch): recall@10=0.842, avg latency 18ms. With microbatch (batch_size=64, microbatch=8, dynamic pad): recall@10=0.815, avg latency 12ms.
Priya Shah: Interesting. 3% absolute drop is non-trivial. Did you quantize for that run?
Alice Nguyen: Yes, run was q4_0 per-channel. We also tried fp16 — microbatching didn't change recall for fp16.
Jon Porter: Could be microbatch-induced ordering of tokens leading to different prefix trimming or KV cache warmup pattern. Also check that microbatching doesn't reorder negative sampling in eval harness.
Priya Shah: I ran a small ablation: same config but shuffled eval queries -> recall@10=0.817 (still down). So ordering only explains a bit.
Alice Nguyen: Config snippet I used:
```
model: azure-embed-lite-v2
quant: q4_0
server:
  microbatch: true
  batch_size: 64
  microbatch_size: 8
  dynamic_padding: true
eval:
  dataset: minibench-10k-holdout
  metric: recall@10
```
Mateo Garcia: Could padding cause different effective sequence lengths and thus different truncation of long docs? If embeddings are computed on truncated contexts, that can change nearest neighbors.
Jon Porter: Also check float drift in quant kernels when aggregating within microbatches vs single forward — accumulation order matters for some kernels.
Priya Shah: I'll run: (1) microbatch on/off with identical quant kernel seeds, (2) microbatch with deterministic padding per example, (3) check embedding norm distributions.
ops-bot: deploy-diff-checker: job 98764 queued for evaluation cluster (tags: microbatch, azure-embed-lite-v2)
Alice Nguyen: Thanks. If embedding norms shift that's a smoking gun. Mateo/Jon — if you see any kernel-level nondeterminism logs (nan, denorm), ping here.
Mateo Garcia: Will do. I'll also export 1k embedding pairs and run cosine delta histogram. Share results in ~30m.
Alice Nguyen: Great — if we confirm it's quant aggregation/order related we might be able to preserve latency win while recovering recall by switching microbatch reduce order or using fp32 accumulators for final norm.
